system:
You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

Return JSON only:
{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",

 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

response: {"headline": "HPS2-THRIVE (25,673 patients, 3.9-year median follow-up) failed to meet its primary endpoint of Major Vascular Event; the niacin/laropiprant mechanism lacks genetic support and its primary biomarker (HDL-C) is non-causal, with a safety signal of increased non-fatal serious adverse events.", "summary": "The HPS2-THRIVE trial randomized 25,673 high-risk vascular disease patients on statin therapy to extended-release niacin/laropiprant (TREDAPTIVE) or placebo and followed them for a median of 3.9 years. The study did not meet its primary endpoint — a composite of coronary death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, stroke, or revascularization (Major Vascular Event). The trial calculator assigns target_genetics = uncertain for niacin's molecular target (GPR109A/HM74A) and treats HDL-C as non-causal, yielding an expected hazard ratio of 1.0 and causal relative risk reduction of 0.0%. Phase 2 data showed a placebo-adjusted HDL-C increase of ~10.4% (ERN/LRPT 19.6% minus placebo 9.2%), but this biomarker change did not translate into clinical benefit. A safety signal was reported (statistically significant increase in some types of non-fatal serious adverse events). Confidence in this assessment is high.", "key_evidence": ["25,673 patients randomized (Merck Announces HPS2-THRIVE Study of TREDAPTIVE (Extended-Release Niacin/Laropiprant) Did Not Achieve Primary Endpoint; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00461630 HPS2-THRIVE)", "Median follow-up 3.9 years (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00461630 HPS2-THRIVE; Merck Announces HPS2-THRIVE Study of TREDAPTIVE (Extended-Release Niacin/Laropiprant) Did Not Achieve Primary Endpoint)", "Primary endpoint: Major Vascular Event — combination of coronary deaths, non-fatal heart attacks, strokes or revascularizations (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00461630 HPS2-THRIVE; Merck Announces HPS2-THRIVE Study of TREDAPTIVE (Extended-Release Niacin/Laropiprant) Did Not Achieve Primary Endpoint)", "Phase 2 placebo-adjusted HDL-C increase ~10.4% (ERN/LRPT 19.6% minus placebo 9.2%) (Effectiveness and safety of laropiprant on niacin-induced flushing)", "Calculator: expected HR 1.0, causal RRR 0.0%, category biomarker_not_causal, weakest_link target genetics: uncertain (calculator)", "Safety signal reported: statistically significant increase in some types of non-fatal serious adverse events (Merck Announces HPS2-THRIVE Study of TREDAPTIVE (Extended-Release Niacin/Laropiprant) Did Not Achieve Primary Endpoint)", "Trial not stopped early, completed as planned (Merck Announces HPS2-THRIVE Study of TREDAPTIVE (Extended-Release Niacin/Laropiprant) Did Not Achieve Primary Endpoint)"], "what_would_change_this": "Placebo-adjusted LDL-C and triglyceride changes from the HPS2-THRIVE phase 3 trial to quantify any causal lipid effect; detailed safety data from the final publication (infections, bleeding, diabetes incidence, discontinuation rates) to assess net clinical harm; human genetic studies of GPR109A variants and CVD outcomes.", "readthrough_note": "The failure of HPS2-THRIVE, together with AIM-HIGH, reinforces that raising HDL-C pharmacologically does not reduce cardiovascular events when LDL-C is already well-controlled. Future programmes targeting HDL-C (e.g., CETP inhibitors) should require genetic validation of the target and demonstration of causal lipid effects beyond HDL-C."}
